entities.summary:
Benedetto Briosco (c.1460–c.1517) was a prominent Italian Renaissance sculptor and architect, active in Lombardy. 

Born in the late 15th century, Briosco is known for his contributions to the development of Mannerist sculpture and architecture in Northern Italy. 

His notable works include the sculpture 'The Madonna of the Rocks' and several architectural projects in Milan and Pavia. 

Briosco's work had a lasting impact on the artistic and architectural landscape of Lombardy, influencing later generations of artists and architects.

He is considered one of the leading figures of the Lombardy Renaissance, a movement that sought to revive classical ideals in the face of the growing influence of the Holy Roman Empire.

Briosco's legacy extends beyond his own work, as he played a significant role in the development of the Renaissance humanist movement in Italy.

In the context of the Renaissance, Briosco's work exemplifies the cultural and artistic exchange between the Italian city-states and the wider European world.
